chunks: O you who believe, when you converse privately, do not talk of iniquity, rebellion, and disobedience to the Prophet, but talk of goodness and piety, and fear God before whom you will be gathered.

key_terms.تَنَاجَيْتُمْ: private conversation or whispering among a few people

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of private conversation mentioned in the Quran for believers?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the incident of the 'Companions of the Cave' (Ashab al-Kahf) or the specific private consultations of the Prophet's wives, highlighting the transition from informal private discourse to structured communal ethics. It establishes a spiritual hierarchy for social interaction, where 'al-birr' (righteousness) and 'al-taqwa' (piety) are not merely individual virtues but communal obligations during private deliberations. The verse underscores that private conversations are never truly private in the divine sense, as they are subject to the same moral scrutiny as public acts.
